bull_case_summary: JPMorgan has $16.9bn normalised quarterly earnings and 23% ROTCE already after observed credit costs. Round two combines these with 14.1% CET1 and deposit growth to defend compensated bank ownership at 13.24x forecast earnings.
bear_case_summary: The bear accepts the purchase thesis and explicitly rejects subtracting existing credit losses twice. Its remaining objections are future credit deterioration, loan-growth exposure, funding repricing and unconfirmed short-term recovery.
key_points_of_agreement: Normalised returns already absorb current credit costs.
Capital and franchise growth are quantified.
Headline gains are excluded and ex-markets NII gives a cleaner funding comparison.
key_points_of_disagreement: How far current returns and capital compensate future adverse-cycle and deposit-cost sensitivity, particularly for aggressive adding.
unresolved_uncertainties: Future card/loan credit trajectory as lending expands.
Funding repricing and persistence of normalised returns through the cycle.
